guides.title: Homo neanderthalensis: Every Mapped Fossil & aDNA Locality Across Eurasia
guides.description: Comprehensive Eurasian atlas of 121 confirmed Neanderthal skeletal, dental, and ancient-DNA localities from Portugal, Gibraltar, Wales, and submerged Doggerland across Europe, Crimea, Caucasus, Levant, and Zagros to Uzbekistan and Altai Siberia (~430–37 ka).
guides.intro: For roughly 400,000 years, Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis) inhabited an immense Eurasian belt stretching nearly 7,000 km from Atlantic Portugal and Wales to Siberia's Altai Mountains, and south to Gibraltar, Sicily/Calabria, Crete-adjacent Mani, Shukbah in Palestine, and the Iranian Zagros. Here we catalogue 121 major and regional confirmed skeletal, dental, and genetic localities across 11 provinces—separating verified human remains from purely lithic Mousterian scatter sites.
guides.scope: All 121 mapped confirmed Neanderthal fossil and ancient-DNA localities across Western Europe, Central/Eastern Europe, Balkans, Crimea, Caucasus, Anatolia, Levant, Zagros, Central Asia, and Altai Siberia (~430–37 ka).

sections.heading: Emergence & Accretion: Sima de los Huesos to MIS 5e (430–120 ka)

paragraphs.text: Neanderthal nuclear DNA divergence from Denisovans dates deep into the Middle Pleistocene (>430 ka): Sima de los Huesos in northern Spain already carries early Neanderthal nuclear DNA and derived mandibles by 430 ka, accompanied by transitional European fossils at Swanscombe (~400 ka), Steinheim (~300–250 ka), Saccopastore (~250 ka MIS 7), Pontnewydd (~225 ka), Biache-Saint-Vaast and Tourville-la-Rivière (~200 ka), Ehringsdorf (~230 ka), and early Southwest Asian teeth at Qaleh Kurd (Iran) and Tabun.

By ~172–115 ka, calcified skeletons like Altamura Man (Apulia, Italy), >800 Krapina bones (Croatia, preserving white-tailed eagle talons crafted into ornaments), Scladina (Belgium, 127 ka), Hohlenstein-Stadel (Germany, 124 ka carrying an ancient ~270 ka introgressed African mtDNA lineage), Baume Moula-Guercy (~120 ka), and Stajnia (~116 ka north of the Carpathians) prove classic Neanderthals thrived across temperate interglacial Europe and simultaneously reached Denisova Cave (~120 ka Denisova 5) in Altai Siberia.

sections.heading: Classic & Eastern Dispersals: Iberia & Doggerland to Crimea, Levant, Zagros & Altai (100–45 ka)

paragraphs.text: During MIS 5–3 glacial cycles, Neanderthals adapted across extraordinarily diverse habitats: coastal marine foraging along Portugal (Figueira Brava, Oliveira), Gibraltar, Italy (Guattari, Cavallo, Archi), and submerged Doggerland plains ('Krijn' dredged from the North Sea floor); alpine Jura caves (Cotencher); tundra hunting at 52°N Salzgitter; intentional pit burials across SW France (La Chapelle-aux-Saints, La Ferrassie, Le Moustier, Regourdou), Syria (Dederiyeh infants), Iraq (Shanidar 1–10 & Shanidar Z), Mount Carmel/Galilee (Kebara hyoid, Amud 1), open-air 'Ein Qashish, and southernmost Shukbah in Palestine.

Across Eastern Europe and Asia, two profound discoveries link geographically vast regions: (1) Pigott et al. (2025 PNAS) extracted an unexpected ~46 ka Neanderthal femur mitogenome from Starosele in Crimea closely matching Micoquian groups >3,000 km away at Chagyrskaya and Okladnikov in Siberia, confirming a rapid ~65–50 ka steppe migration alongside Teshik-Tash (Uzbekistan) and North Caucasus Mezmaiskaya; and (2) genetic evidence at Denisova 11 ('Denny', an F1 Neanderthal–Denisovan daughter) documents inter-lineage encounters at Eurasian crossroads.

sections.heading: Demographic Isolation, Overlap & Disappearance (~45–38 ka) — Scope Note on Minor Fragments

paragraphs.text: High-resolution hydroxyproline radiocarbon dating (Spy/Engis/Goyet ~44–40.6 ka, Vindija ~44–42 ka, Subalyuk ~40 ka, Sima de las Palomas ~43–40 ka, Bawa Yawan ~43–41 ka) combined with 2024 genomic sequencing of 'Thorin' from Grotte Mandrin (50,000 years isolated from contemporary late French groups!) reveals that final European Neanderthal populations splintered into tiny, genetically isolated pockets prior to ~40–39 ka, even as arriving Homo sapiens incorporated ~2% Neanderthal ancestry (captured directly in ~40 ka Peștera cu Oase 1 in Romania).

Transparency on scope: This atlas maps every major and regionally diagnostic confirmed Neanderthal skeletal, dental, and aDNA locality (121 named sites). Hundreds of additional tiny single-tooth museum fragments without firm stratigraphic dates (mostly within already mapped Dordogne/Charente/Belgian/Italian river valleys) and >1,000 purely stone-tool Mousterian sites lacking human bones are intentionally kept distinct from confirmed fossil sites.

cells: Qaleh Kurd Cave (Qazvin, Iranian Central Plateau)
c. 450,000–150,000 years ago (Middle Pleistocene) (Electron spin resonance and uranium-series dating on horse teeth associated with an archaic Homo deciduous canine on the Iranian Plateau.)
Establishes the oldest securely dated stratified hominin fossil and Mousterian-like hunted equid assemblage on the Iranian Central Plateau east of the Zagros.
A single deciduous tooth leaves fine species resolution between H. heidelbergensis and early Neanderthals open.
Sima de los Huesos

About 430 ka (Rounded geological age of the fossil assemblage; DNA gives affinity rather than a direct date. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.)
Nuclear DNA places the Sima hominins on the Neanderthal side of the Neanderthal–Denisovan division.
Their mitochondrial affinity differs; one maternal lineage cannot stand in for the population history. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.
Barnfield Pit, Swanscombe (Kent, England)
c. 400 thousand years ago (MIS 11 Hoxnian) (Biostratigraphy, amino-acid racemization, and Hoxnian interglacial Thames terrace correlation.)
Three refitting parietal and occipital skull bones of a young woman discovered between 1935 and 1955 showing early incipient Neanderthal occipital traits amid pointed Acheulean handaxes above…
Facial skeleton absent; phylogenetic placement debates stem Neanderthal vs. broader H. heidelbergensis.
Pešturina & Velika/Mala Balanica (Jelašnica Gorge, Serbia)
~400–45 thousand years ago (TL, ESR & Lindal (2020) / Radović (2025 AJPA))
Mala Balanica (~400 ka BH-1 mandible lacking derived Neanderthal traits) and Velika Balanica (~300 ka) contrast with late Pleistocene Pešturina's true Neanderthal molar and bone bearing…
Deeply fractured Balkan karst sequence spans Middle Pleistocene isolation vs Late Pleistocene Neanderthal gene flow.
Tabun Cave & Nahal Meʾarot (Mount Carmel)
c. 350,000–45,000 years ago (Post-IR IRSL (pIRIR290), ESR and TL chronologies spanning 25 metres of Lower Acheulean, Acheulo-Yabrudian and Levantine Mousterian stratigraphy.)
Provides the benchmark Levantine chronological column from Upper Acheulean handaxes through Tabun C1 Neanderthal-affiliated skeletal remains and bird/ungulate Mousterian subsistence.
Diagenetic uranium uptake and historical Garrod-era trench mixing complicate fine sub-layer correlation for older finds.
Cova del Bolomor (Tavernes de la Valldigna, Valencia, Spain)
~350–100 thousand years ago (TL, OSL, ESR/U-series across 17 stratigraphic levels)
Isolated parietals, teeth, and fibula spanning MIS 9 to MIS 5e alongside Europe's clearest early hearths and tortoise/small-game processing.
Small fragmentary hominin fossils span multiple interglacial cycles.
Steinheim an der Murr (Baden-Württemberg, Germany)
~320–240 thousand years ago (Holsteinian/MIS 9–7 terrace stratigraphy & Buzi et al. (2021) retrodeformation)
Remarkably complete crushed adult cranium (Steinheim 1, 1933) exhibiting incipient Neanderthal lambdoid/supraorbital traits alongside more globular midface anatomy—pivotal anchor for the…
Post-depositional compression deformed left side of face prior to digital retrodeformation.
Cova Negra (Xàtiva, Valencia, Spain)
c. 273–146 thousand years ago (OSL, ESR, and micro-CT paleopathology of CN-42170 temporal labyrinth inside Iberian Mousterian levels.)
Multilayered Iberian Neanderthal cave preserving rare inner-ear Down syndrome labyrinth anatomy in an ~6-year-old child who survived well beyond infancy thanks to compassionate collective…
Sparse absolute C14 dates in deep strata rely on combined ESR/OSL sediment series.
Saccopastore 1 & 2 (Aniene River, Rome, Italy)
~255–220 thousand years ago (Revised MIS 7 40Ar/39Ar fluvial terrace dating (Marra et al. 2015 QSR))
Two exceptionally preserved crania (1929 female Saccopastore 1, 1935 male Saccopastore 2) recovered in Roman gravel quarries; 2015 revision pushed them back from MIS 5e to ~250 ka MIS 7,…
Modern urban Rome now overlies the original Aniene gravel pit.
Payre (Rompon, Ardèche, France)
~250–125 thousand years ago (ESR, U-series & Hardy/Moncel (2011, 2020))
Collapsed limestone terrace shelter yielding human teeth and Payre 15 mandible alongside early Levallois/discoid cores with fish scales, avian bones, and starchy plants.
Early Middle Paleolithic transition specimens.
Pontnewydd Cave (Denbighshire, North Wales)
c. 225 thousand years ago (MIS 7) (TL on burned flint, U-series on flowstone, and fauna bracketing volcanic tuff-pebble Levallois tools and taurodont teeth.)
Northernmost MIS 7 European Neanderthal site yielding ~19 taurodont dental & jaw specimens from at least five individuals who shaped volcanic-rock handaxes and Levallois points.
Debris-flow mudslides washed remains deep inside the karst gallery.
La Cotte de St Brelade (Jersey, Channel Islands)
~240–48 thousand years ago (OSL, TL & Compton et al. (2021) JHE dental morphology)
Dramatic granite sea-ravine ambush site preserving mammoth/woolly-rhino stampede cliffs (~240–130 ka) and 13 permanent teeth (1910/1911) recently re-analyzed in 2021 as <48 ka late…
Pre-war 1910–11 trenching separated teeth slightly from later mammoth bonebed levels.
La Niche at Montmaurin (Haute-Garonne, France)
~240–120 thousand years ago (U-series, biostratigraphy & Vialet et al. (2018) PLOS ONE)
Complete adult mandible (Montmaurin-La Niche, MIS 7 ~200–240 ka) with archaic-to-Neanderthal mosaic symphysis and incipient retromolar space bridging Middle Pleistocene lineages into…
Vertical chimney breccia lacked direct radiometric ash.
Biache-Saint-Vaast (Pas-de-Calais, Northern France)
~230–180 thousand years ago (TL, ESR & Martín-Francés et al. (2022))
Two partial skulls (BSV 1 young female, BSV 2 older individual) excavated cleanly from alluvial silt with Levallois points showing unmistakable Neanderthal occipital bunning and inner-ear…
Partial crania without mandibles.
Ehringsdorf & Taubach (Weimar, Thuringia, Germany)
~230–120 thousand years ago (U-series Lower Travertine ~230 ka (Blackwell & Schwarcz 1986) / MIS 5e Taubach)
Adult parietal/mandibles/crania from Ehringsdorf (~230 ka MIS 7 interglacial travertine) showing mixed archaic/derived Neanderthal anatomy plus cut/burnt trauma, paired with MIS 5e ~125 ka…
Commercial travertine quarrying disturbed exact micro-provenance between lower and upper travertines.
Tourville-la-Rivière (Seine-Maritime, Normandy, France)
~220–185 thousand years ago (ESR & U-series fluvial terrace dating (~226–183 ka, Faivre et al. 2014))
Left humerus, ulna, and radius of a young adult (~200 ka MIS 7) beside butchered horse/aurochs carcasses in Seine meander gravels, bearing healed repetitive spear-throwing microtrauma.
Isolated left forelimb without cranium.
Apidima Cave (Mani Peninsula, Greece)
c. 210,000–160,000 years ago (Uranium-series dating and virtual 3D morphometric reconstruction of breccia-embedded Apidima 1 (~210 ka) and Apidima 2 (~170 ka) posterior crania.)
Raises the landmark hypothesis that an early out-of-Africa Homo sapiens dispersal reached southern Greece by ~210,000 years ago before subsequent replacement by late Middle Pleistocene…
No stone tools accompany the sea-cliff breccia pocket, and some specialists caution that post-mortem distortion in Apidima 1 merits conservative species interpretation.
Reilingen (Upper Rhine Valley, Baden-Württemberg, Germany)
~200–130 thousand years ago (Rhine alluvial terrace morphology (Buzi et al. 2021))
Adult occipital, parietals, and right temporal recovered along Upper Rhine gravels displaying classic Neanderthal suprainiac fossa and incipient lambdoid flattening.
Dredged terrace deposit.
Sakajia, Djruchula, Bronze & Bondi Caves (Georgia) & Azokh (Armenia/Caucasus)
~200–40 thousand years ago (TL, ESR & Pleurdeau/Tushabramishvili (2012 JHE))
Dense Georgian Southern Caucasus cluster: Sakajia maxilla/teeth, Djruchula early elongated-blade Mousterian molar (~140–200 ka), Bronze Cave child tooth, Bondi Cave tooth/obsidian, and Lesser…
Small dental collections spanning broad Middle-to-Upper Pleistocene phases.
Bau de l'Aubesier (Vaucluse, Provence, France)
~190–100 thousand years ago (TL burnt-flint dating (~190–140 ka) & Lebel/Trinkaus (2001 PNAS))
Twelve human teeth and the famous Aubesier 11 adult mandible preserving extreme antemortem tooth loss and alveolar resorption proving compassionate caregiving for disabled elders nearly 200…
Mandibular fragments derived from complex Mont Ventoux rockfall deposits.
Grotte du Lazaret (Nice, Maritime Alps, France)
~190–130 thousand years ago (ESR/U-series & marine-terrace stratigraphy)
Over 25 late MIS 6 early Neanderthal cranial fragments, parietals, and teeth found within organized seaweed-bedding habitation floors facing glacial Mediterranean shores.
Pre-Eemian early Neanderthal features complement Suard and Ehringsdorf.
La Chaise-de-Vouthon (Suard & Bourgeois-Delaunay, Charente, France)
~185–110 thousand years ago (U-series speleothems (MIS 6 Abri Suard / MIS 5e Bourgeois-Delaunay) & Zanolli 2020)
Dual adjoining caves preserving 50+ pre-Würm early Neanderthal remains: Suard (MIS 6 ~185–128 ka parietal/teeth) and Bourgeois-Delaunay (MIS 5e ~128–110 ka BD 1 mandible, cranial vault, femur).
Early vs classic Neanderthal mosaic anatomy tracks MIS 6 to MIS 5e transitions.
Altamura Man / Grotta di Lamalunga (Apulia, Italy)
~172–130 thousand years ago (U-Th calcite coralloid dating & Profico et al. (2023 Commun. Biol.))
The most complete early Neanderthal skeleton known globally, still fused by sparkling calcite 'cave popcorn' deep in an underground karst shaft at Altamura; 2015 extraction yielded oldest…
Encrusted in situ under protected UNESCO-style karst rules; only small scapula fragment physically sampled.
Ochtendung & Sarstedt / Warendorf (Germany)
~160–45 thousand years ago (Eifel volcano caldera & NW German gravel pit cranial finds)
Crater-basin skullcap at Ochtendung (East Eifel) alongside Sarstedt and Warendorf cranial vaults anchoring western German plains between Feldhofer and Bavaria.
Quarry/gravel-pit recovery contexts.
Combe-Grenal (Domme, Dordogne, France)
~150–45 thousand years ago (TL, ESR & François Bordes master sequence (Levels 1–65))
Over 65 stratified Mousterian horizons preserving classic Neanderthal teeth, mandibular fragments, and cutmarked bone documenting climate-driven shifts between Quina, Ferrassie, and…
Sparse hominin bone count relative to vast lithic/faunal recovery.
Fontéchevade (Montbron, Charente, France)
~150–40 thousand years ago (Chase et al. (2009) ESR/OSL & radiocarbon revision)
Historically misinterpreted in 1947 as evidence of an ancient 'pre-sapiens' vault without browridges (Fontéchevade II); modern micro-CT/redating confirmed classic Neanderthal affinities…
Mixed cave-roof breccias complicated 1947 age assignment.
Krapina (Hušnjakovo Rock Shelter, Croatia)
c. 135,000–120,000 years ago (MIS 5e) (ESR and U-series dating of sandstone shelter deposits yielding >800 remains of dozens of Neanderthals and polished/cutmarks on white-tailed eagle talons.)
Forms Europe’s largest single-site Neanderthal skeletal sample (~130 ka), exhibiting healing injuries, stone-tool cutmarks and curated white-tailed sea eagle talons interpreted as personal…
1899–1905 Gorjanović-Kramberger stratigraphic records predate modern micro-taphonomic provenance mapping.
Baume Moula-Guercy (Soyons, Ardèche, France)
~130–105 thousand years ago (TL, paleosol MIS 5e & Richards et al. (2021–2024) cranial/mandibular studies)
Minimum 6 individuals (>120 bones of adults, adolescents, children) defleshed, disarticulated, and marrow-cracked in Layer XV during Last Interglacial temperate woodland maxima.
Endocannibalism vs dietary stress during rapid woodland biome change remains debated.
Denisova Cave East Chamber (Altai, Siberia)
~130–90 thousand years ago (OSL, U-Th & Prüfer/Massilani (2014–2026) high-coverage nuclear genome)
Adult female pedal phalanx (Denisova 5, East Chamber Layer 11.4, ~120 ka) delivering the foundational high-coverage 'Altai Neanderthal' nuclear genome revealing high inbreeding (half-sibling…
Co-occupied the same cave system intermittently with Denisovans across ~200 kyr.
Hohlenstein-Stadel (Lone Valley, Swabian Jura, Germany)
~130–115 thousand years ago (Posth et al. (2017 Nature Comm.) molecular clock & Peyrégne (2019))
Isolated 124 ka right femoral shaft ('HST') carrying an extraordinarily divergent mitochondrial haplotype splitting ~270 ka from other Neanderthals—implying an early African gene flow into…
Only a carnivore-gnawed femur shaft preserved in basal Mousterian layer.
Lezetxiki Cave (Arrasate, Gipuzkoa, Spain)
~130–45 thousand years ago (U-series, ESR & 2023 AJPA micro-CT dental reassessment (López-Onaindia))
Adult female humerus (1964) and molar/premolar teeth along the Atlantic Cantabrian corridor showing strong classic Neanderthal internal enamel morphology.
Complex breccia stratigraphy separated humerus (~MIS 6/5) from upper Mousterian teeth.
Scladina Cave (Sclayn, Andenne, Belgium)
~130–120 thousand years ago (Gamma spectrometry, TL & Peyrégne et al. (2019 Sci. Adv.) nuclear genome)
Right mandible, maxilla, and 16 teeth of an 8-year-old child (~127 ka Unit 4A) providing the oldest Belgian nuclear genome, linking early Western European Neanderthals to later 40 ka…
Disarticulated juvenile jaw fragments in flowstone/alluvial clay.
Barakaevskaya & Matuzka / Monasheskaya Caves (North Caucasus, Russia)
~120–45 thousand years ago (Doronicheva et al. (2023 PLOS ONE) & Liubin Caucasus excavations)
Child mandible (Barakaevskaya), isolated molars (Monasheskaya, Matuzka) spanning Kuban highland Micoquian & Zagros-like facies across the northern slope of the Greater Caucasus.
Fragmentary isolated child mandibles/teeth.
Ciemna Cave (Ojców National Park, Poland)
~120–100 thousand years ago (OSL & Willman et al. (2019 J. Paleol. Archaeol.))
Neanderthal deciduous molar and two child manual phalanges bearing acid digestion pitting (probably passed through a giant bird's digestive tract—one of Europe's rarest taphonomic findings!).
Isolated pediatric elements in MIS 5c–5a loessy sediments.
Gánovce (Poprad) & Šaľa (Slovakia)
~120–70 thousand years ago (U-series MIS 5e travertine & Eisová et al. (2019) paleoneurology)
Natural calcite mineral endocast preserving cortical convolutions inside MIS 5e–5d travertine at Gánovce (~105 ka) plus Šaľa 1 & 2 frontals/parietal dredged from Váh River gravels in western…
Travertine cast preserves external brain/meningeal anatomy without intact cranial bone table.
Karain Cave E (Antalya, SW Turkey)
~120–60 thousand years ago (ESR, U-series & Mediterranean Anatolia excavations)
Multi-chamber Taurus foothills karst site preserving Neanderthal teeth and postcranial shafts inside thick Zagros/Levantine-style Mousterian travertines bridging the Levant and Balkans.
Older early excavations partially mixed transitional upper boundaries.
Stajnia Cave (Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, Poland)
~120–45 thousand years ago (U-series, aDNA molecular clock & Picin et al. (2020 Sci. Rep.; 2026 Curr. Biol.))
Three Neanderthal molars including S5000 (~116–82 ka) yielding the oldest central/eastern European Neanderthal mtDNA genome and showing multi-individual maternal turnover linking Poland with…
Isolated teeth excavated with Micoquian bifacial knives in periglacial cave silt.
Gruta da Figueira Brava (Setúbal, Portugal)
c. 106–86 thousand years ago (MIS 5c–5b) (U-series and OSL dating on coastal karst cave chambers rich in charred brown-crab claws, pine nuts, and limpets.)
Conclusive Atlantic coastal evidence proving Last Interglacial Neanderthals systematically harvested roasted brown crabs, mussels, limpets, seals, seabirds, and roasted stone-pine…
Post-glacial sea-level rise flooded lower outer coastal caves across the same Arrábida cliff.
Gorham’s & Vanguard Caves (Gibraltar)
c. 100,000–30,000 years ago (OSL/radiocarbon chronologies of Mousterian coastal middens (monk seal, dolphin, Limpet shells), raptor-feather cutmarks and bedrock geometric hatchings.)
Sea-level coastal caves at the Strait of Gibraltar show Neanderthals harvesting coastal marine resources, capturing corvid/raptor wing feathers, distilling birch/rockrose tar in small hearths…
Late persistence debates (<32 ka) remain sensitive to subtle radiocarbon contamination filtering.
Gruta da Oliveira (Almonda Karst, Portugal)
~100–45 thousand years ago (U-series, TL, OSL & radiocarbon stratigraphy)
Phalanges, metacarpals, cranial fragments, and teeth (Oliveira 1–10) from structured hearths in Zilhão's Almonda karst sequence near Torres Novas.
Fragmentary postcranial/dental elements span Mousterian Layers 8–22.
Kalamakia & Lakonis Caves (Mani Peninsula, Greece)
~100–40 thousand years ago (ESR, U-series, OSL & Panagopoulou (2002) / Harvati (2013))
Fourteen Neanderthal teeth and cranial fragments from Kalamakia (~100–40 ka) plus a strontium-isotope mobile ~44–40 ka Neanderthal molar from Lakonis I, proving southern Greece served as a…
Submerged lower coastal karst shelves conceal additional Pleistocene shore camps.
Pinilla del Valle / Calvero de la Higuera (Madrid, Spain)
~95–42 thousand years ago (TL, OSL & U-series across Camino, Buena Pinta & Navalmaíllo caves)
Neanderthal molars (Camino & Buena Pinta caves) plus Des-Cubierta child burial-linked symbolic horned skulls accumulation in Guadarrama highlands.
Carnivore modification mixed some hyena-den assemblages at Camino.
Denisova 11

About 90 ka; molecular estimate (Approximate genetic age used in the 2018 study; direct radiocarbon established only older than 50 ka. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.)
A female’s nuclear genome identifies a Neanderthal mother and Denisovan father.

The rounded molecular age is model dependent; a fossil location does not establish where her parents met or whether she had descendants. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.
Obi-Rakhmat Grotto (Paltau Valley, Tashkent, Uzbekistan)
~90–60 thousand years ago (U-series, ESR & Glantz et al. (2008 JHE) / Krivoshapkin (2010))
Over 150 cranial fragments and six maxillary teeth (OR-1, ~9–12-year-old child) pairing classic Neanderthal huge dentition with atypically thin, high/globular parietal vaults along the Tian…
No nuclear DNA extracted yet from OR-1 to distinguish archaic drift from introgression.
Archi (Calabria) & Grotta di Santa Croce (Bisceglie, Apulia, Italy)
~80–40 thousand years ago (Histology & southern Italian Neanderthal catalogue (Sci. Rep. 2021))
Archi 1 child mandible (~45 ka near Strait of Messina) and Santa Croce adult femur (Apulia) documenting Neanderthals at the southernmost toe of mainland Italy.

Quarrying destroyed the original limestone cliff in 1856; all context stems from sediment screening & direct 14C/aDNA.

Minor stratigraphic mixing debate between underlying Denticulate Mousterian and Châtelperronian units.
Spy Cave (Betch aux Rotches, Namur, Belgium)
~44–40.5 thousand years ago (Devièse et al. (2021 PNAS) hydroxyproline single-amino-acid 14C)
Discovered in 1886, Spy I and Spy II proved scientifically that Neanderthals were truly fossil Pleistocene humans buried with cold-steppe fauna and Mousterian tools; 2021 compound-specific…
